purpose: Provide an evaluable work-unit ontology for writing Pythonic code, typing and testing it, managing environments and dependencies, and packaging, versioning, and publishing Python software and libraries, as a knowledge-searcher subdomain node about where and how to do this work correctly.
assumptions: Scope is the Python language and ecosystem for shipping software; nodes are concrete engineering work-units.
No observed dataset or benchmark supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors.
Targets modern packaging standards (pyproject.toml, PEP 517/518 build backends, wheels/sdists).
Both application and library packaging are in scope; dependency strategy differs by that classification.
exclusions: Language-internals/CPython implementation and C-extension build toolchains beyond declaring them.
Non-Python packaging ecosystems (conda/system package managers) except as contrast.
Web frameworks, data science, and async runtime concerns except where they touch packaging.
Operational deployment, containerization, and runtime monitoring after publish.

competency_questions.question: What project scope and source layout should be fixed before any packaging work begins?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROJECT_SCOPE_LAYOUT present and early in workflow

competency_questions.question: Which Pythonic language constructs make a class or pipeline idiomatic and protocol-conformant?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: data-model, iterator, comprehension, decorator, context-manager nodes present

competency_questions.question: How are interface contracts typed and how is static type checking gated in CI?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TYPE_HINTS_DESIGN and STATIC_TYPE_CHECK present with a dependency edge

competency_questions.question: How is behavior tested, isolated, driven, and measured for quality?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: pytest, fixtures, TDD, coverage nodes present

competency_questions.question: How are isolated environments, dependency constraints, resolution, and lockfiles managed for reproducibility?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: venv, resolution, lockfile, tooling nodes present

competency_questions.question: What metadata and build steps produce installable wheels/sdists with correct entry points?
How are versions assigned and artifacts published safely to an index?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEMANTIC_VERSIONING and PYPI_PUBLISHING present with gating edges

competency_questions.question: How is the whole pipeline automated so every release is validated identically?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CI_RELEASE_AUTOMATION present and depends on test/type/build/publish

competency_questions.question: Which work units are irreversible or high-risk and therefore require human review before finalizing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: high-risk nodes carry human_review_required and acceptance_tests

competency_questions.question: What is the correct execution order that minimizes packaging rework?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: priority_order lists every node respecting dependencies

competency_questions.question: How is the dependency/packaging toolchain selected and standardized across a team?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ENV_TOOLING_SELECTION present with a tooling-vs-standard conflict axis

competency_questions.question: How is the freshness-versus-reproducibility tradeoff resolved for dependencies?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: a freshness-vs-lock conflict axis with dominance logic exists

competency_questions.question: How does a defective published release trigger correction without mutating the published version?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: a feedback edge from publish to versioning with a stop condition exists

competency_questions.question: How is QA effort balanced between static typing and behavioral testing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: a typing-vs-testing conflict axis with a resolution rule exists

glossary.definition: a built, installable Python distribution archive (.whl) requiring no build step on install
a source distribution archive containing the files needed to build a wheel
the standardized declarative file holding project metadata and the build-system table
a file pinning the fully resolved dependency graph with versions and hashes for reproducible installs
an isolated per-project interpreter and library directory
a declared name mapping (e.g. console script or plugin) discoverable after installation
a version scheme where MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH signals breaking/feature/fix changes
an annotation expressing the expected type contract of a name or interface
a pytest-provided, scoped test dependency with setup and teardown
an object implementing __enter__/__exit__ for deterministic resource handling
the PEP 517 tool that turns source into wheels/sdists, selected in pyproject

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established Python ecosystem and packaging practice and literature (Ramalho 'Fluent Python'; Slatkin 'Effective Python'; Beazley & Jones 'Python Cookbook'; PyPA packaging guides and PEP 517/518/621/440 conventions); no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Decide the project's purpose, public API surface, and source tree layout (src-layout vs flat, package vs module) before code or packaging metadata is written.
contradictors: developer who codes before deciding layout

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the product reclassifies app vs library or the public API surface is renamed

pros.claim: a stable layout and API surface anchors every downstream packaging decision
pros.example: src-layout prevents importing the in-tree copy during tests

cons.claim: premature layout lock forces rework of imports and entry points
cons.example: switching flat->src after release breaks editable installs

failure_modes: flat layout shadows installed package in tests
acceptance_tests: src vs flat layout decision recorded with rationale
public API surface enumerated in a stable list

nodes.definition: Implement classes using the Python data model (dunder methods, descriptors, __slots__) so objects integrate with built-in protocols and idioms.
contradictors: developer who reimplements built-in protocols by hand

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a class must support a new protocol or built-in behavior

pros.claim: correct dunder methods make objects behave like built-ins and compose with stdlib
pros.example: __eq__/__hash__ pair lets objects be dict keys safely

cons.claim: partial protocol implementation yields surprising runtime behavior
cons.example: defining __eq__ without __hash__ makes instances unhashable

nodes.definition: Express lazy sequences and pipelines with the iterator protocol, generator functions, and generator expressions instead of materializing intermediate lists.
contradictors: developer who always builds full lists in memory

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when memory pressure or streaming requirements change

pros.claim: generators bound memory and enable infinite/streaming pipelines
pros.example: yield from chains generators without buffering

cons.claim: single-use iterators silently exhaust and confuse callers
cons.example: reusing an exhausted generator yields nothing

nodes.definition: Use comprehensions, unpacking, and core idioms to express transformations concisely while keeping them readable and side-effect free.
contradictors: developer porting C-style loops verbatim

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a comprehension grows too complex to read

pros.claim: comprehensions express intent more clearly than manual loops
pros.example: a dict comprehension builds a lookup in one expression

cons.claim: overlong nested comprehensions hurt readability
cons.example: triple-nested comprehension obscures logic

nodes.definition: Build reusable cross-cutting behavior with closures and decorators while preserving wrapped function metadata and signatures.
contradictors: developer who copies cross-cutting code into each function

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a decorator must preserve a new aspect of the wrapped callable

pros.claim: decorators factor cross-cutting concerns out of business logic
pros.example: functools.wraps preserves __name__ and __doc__

cons.claim: decorators that drop metadata break introspection and tooling
cons.example: missing wraps hides the real signature from help()

nodes.definition: Manage acquisition and deterministic release of resources via context managers (with-statement, contextlib) instead of manual try/finally scattering.
contradictors: developer who leaks file/socket handles

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a new resource type needs deterministic cleanup

pros.claim: context managers guarantee cleanup even on exceptions
pros.example: with open(...) closes the file on any exit path

cons.claim: hand-rolled try/finally is easy to get wrong under nesting
cons.example: forgotten finally leaks a lock on error

nodes.definition: Annotate public and internal interfaces with type hints (generics, Protocols, typing constructs) that express real contracts and aid tooling.
contradictors: developer who treats type hints as decoration only

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the public API or data contracts change shape

pros.claim: precise hints catch interface errors before runtime and document contracts
pros.example: a Protocol expresses structural typing for duck-typed inputs

cons.claim: over- or mis-annotation gives false confidence and fights the type checker
cons.example: Any everywhere defeats the purpose of typing

failure_modes: Any used to silence real errors
revisit_triggers: public-API annotations re-reviewed when API surface changes

nodes.definition: Configure and run a static type checker (mypy/pyright) with a chosen strictness so type errors are caught in CI rather than production.
contradictors: developer who never runs the type checker

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when strictness level or checker version changes results

pros.claim: a CI type gate prevents whole classes of interface bugs
pros.example: mypy --strict flags a None that would crash at runtime

cons.claim: unrealistic strictness floods the team with low-value errors
cons.example: strict mode on untyped deps yields noise via missing stubs

failure_modes: strictness mismatch between local and CI

nodes.definition: Design a pytest suite (test discovery, assertions, parametrization, markers) that exercises behavior at appropriate granularity.
contradictors: developer who only tests manually

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when behavior or public API changes and tests must follow

pros.claim: a behavior-focused pytest suite catches regressions cheaply
pros.example: parametrize tests one function across many input/expected pairs

cons.claim: tests coupled to implementation break on harmless refactors
cons.example: asserting on private internals fails on every refactor

failure_modes: tests assert on internals not behavior
revisit_triggers: test suite re-examined when public behavior changes

nodes.definition: Provide test dependencies and isolation through pytest fixtures with correct scope and teardown so tests are deterministic and independent.
contradictors: developer who shares mutable global state across tests

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when shared state or fixture scope causes cross-test interference

pros.claim: correctly scoped fixtures isolate tests and prevent order-dependence
pros.example: a function-scoped tmp_path gives each test a clean directory

cons.claim: wrong fixture scope leaks state and creates flaky, order-dependent tests
cons.example: a session-scoped mutable fixture couples unrelated tests

failure_modes: fixture scope too broad leaks state

nodes.definition: Drive design with a red-green-refactor loop so tests specify behavior before implementation and refactoring stays safe.
contradictors: developer who writes tests only after shipping

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when requirements shift mid-implementation

pros.claim: writing the test first clarifies the contract and prevents over-building
pros.example: a failing test for empty input forces explicit edge handling

cons.claim: dogmatic TDD on exploratory spikes slows discovery
cons.example: strict TDD on a throwaway prototype wastes effort

failure_modes: tests written to pass not to specify

nodes.definition: Measure and interpret test coverage and quality signals to find untested risk without chasing a coverage number for its own sake.
contradictors: manager who mandates 100% coverage blindly

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when coverage drops or hides untested critical paths

pros.claim: coverage gaps reveal untested risk areas to prioritize
pros.example: branch coverage exposes an unhandled exception path

cons.claim: high line coverage gives false assurance without good assertions
cons.example: 100% coverage with weak asserts still misses bugs

failure_modes: coverage chased as a vanity metric

nodes.definition: Create isolated per-project interpreters and environments (venv/virtualenv) so project dependencies do not collide globally.
contradictors: developer who pip-installs into the system Python

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the target interpreter version or isolation boundary changes

pros.claim: per-project isolation prevents dependency collisions and 'works on my machine'
pros.example: venv keeps two projects on different library versions

cons.claim: forgetting to activate installs into the wrong interpreter
cons.example: pip install hits system Python when venv not activated

failure_modes: installed into system python by mistake
stale env not rebuilt after python upgrade
revisit_triggers: env strategy revisited when interpreter or isolation policy changes

nodes.definition: Declare dependencies with version constraints and let a resolver compute a compatible set, balancing freshness against stability.
contradictors: developer who installs latest of everything unpinned

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a dependency conflict or security advisory forces constraint changes

pros.claim: explicit constraints make resolution predictable and auditable
pros.example: an upper bound avoids a known-breaking major bump

cons.claim: over-tight or over-loose constraints cause unsolvable or unstable resolutions
cons.example: conflicting pins make the resolver fail to find a set

revisit_triggers: constraints re-reviewed on conflict or advisory

nodes.definition: Pin the fully resolved dependency graph in a lockfile (with hashes) so environments rebuild identically across machines and time.
contradictors: developer who never commits a lockfile

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the lockfile diverges from the manifest or a hash check fails

pros.claim: a hashed lockfile makes builds byte-reproducible and tamper-evident
pros.example: pinned hashes block a swapped malicious artifact

cons.claim: stale lockfiles silently ship outdated or vulnerable versions
cons.example: an unupdated lock keeps a CVE-affected pin

failure_modes: lockfile out of sync with manifest
acceptance_tests: lockfile regenerated from the current manifest only

nodes.definition: Choose and standardize the dependency/packaging toolchain (pip+venv vs poetry vs uv) given team, speed, and lockfile needs.
contradictors: developer who mixes incompatible tools per machine

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when tool capabilities, speed, or ecosystem support shift materially

pros.claim: one standardized toolchain removes per-developer drift
pros.example: whole team on uv gets identical fast resolves

cons.claim: premature tool lock-in is costly to reverse across a team
cons.example: migrating a large repo off poetry mid-project is disruptive

nodes.definition: Author pyproject.toml: project metadata, dependencies, and the build-system table selecting a PEP 517 backend.
contradictors: developer clinging to legacy setup.py only

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when metadata standards, build backend, or dependency declarations change

pros.claim: pyproject.toml is the single standardized source of build metadata
pros.example: [build-system] selects hatchling/setuptools declaratively

cons.claim: malformed or incomplete metadata breaks builds and installs downstream
cons.example: a missing build-backend makes the project unbuildable

failure_modes: invalid TOML or missing build-system table
metadata duplicated across setup.py and pyproject
acceptance_tests: pyproject.toml parses and declares name, version, and build-system
dependencies declared once, not duplicated in setup.py

nodes.definition: Produce the distribution artifacts: a source distribution (sdist) and one or more wheels via the declared build backend.
contradictors: developer who ships raw source folders

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the build backend, included files, or wheel tags change

pros.claim: wheels install fast without a build step and sdists preserve buildability
pros.example: a pure-python wheel installs with no compiler needed

cons.claim: misconfigured builds omit files or produce broken wheels
cons.example: missing package data ships a wheel that fails at import

failure_modes: sdist missing files needed to rebuild
acceptance_tests: built wheel installs into a clean venv and imports

nodes.definition: Declare console scripts, plugin entry points, optional extras, and package data so installed distributions expose the right interfaces.
contradictors: developer who tells users to run scripts by path

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when CLI commands, plugin contracts, or extras change

pros.claim: entry points expose CLIs and plugins through a standard discovery mechanism
pros.example: a console_scripts entry point installs a runnable command

cons.claim: wrong entry-point or extras config hides functionality from installers
cons.example: a typo'd console script installs no command

failure_modes: entry point references a missing callable

nodes.definition: Assign versions under a semantic-versioning policy that signals breaking vs compatible changes to consumers and tooling.
contradictors: maintainer who bumps versions arbitrarily

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a change alters the public API or breaks compatibility

pros.claim: semver lets consumers and resolvers reason about safe upgrades
pros.example: a major bump warns that imports may break

cons.claim: mislabeling a breaking change as minor silently breaks downstreams
cons.example: a renamed function shipped as a patch breaks importers

failure_modes: breaking change shipped under a non-major bump
acceptance_tests: public API diff reviewed before assigning the bump level
breaking changes mapped to a major increment

nodes.definition: Upload validated artifacts to an index (TestPyPI then PyPI) using trusted publishing/secure tokens, after metadata and install checks pass.
contradictors: developer who uploads untested artifacts directly to PyPI

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a release is found defective and a new version must supersede it

pros.claim: a gated publish with trusted publishing prevents leaked tokens and bad releases
pros.example: TestPyPI dry-run catches metadata errors before the real upload

cons.claim: a published version is immutable, so mistakes cannot be overwritten
cons.example: a broken 1.0.0 cannot be replaced, only yanked and superseded

acceptance_tests: TestPyPI upload and install succeed before PyPI
release uses trusted publishing or scoped token
revisit_triggers: index policy or credential mechanism changes

nodes.definition: Automate test, type-check, build, and publish in CI so every release runs the same validated, reproducible pipeline.
contradictors: developer who builds and uploads manually from a laptop

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when pipeline steps, runners, or secrets handling change

pros.claim: CI runs the identical validated pipeline for every release
pros.example: a tagged commit triggers test-build-publish with no manual steps

cons.claim: a gap in the pipeline lets unvalidated artifacts reach users
cons.example: skipping the type gate in CI ships an interface regression

revisit_triggers: pipeline re-reviewed when steps, runners, or secret handling change

edges.why_related: layout and API surface fix what classes must model
edges.risk_of_conflict: designing classes before scope churns them

edges.why_related: iterator protocol builds on the data model
edges.risk_of_conflict: writing generators before the protocol model is clear causes rework

edges.why_related: comprehensions are a concise form over iteration
edges.risk_of_conflict: idioms chosen before grasping laziness misuse memory

edges.why_related: decorators wrap callables defined under the data model
edges.risk_of_conflict: decorating before stable callables churns wrappers

edges.why_related: context managers are a data-model protocol
edges.risk_of_conflict: resource code before protocol grasp leaks handles

edges.why_related: the public API surface defines what to type
edges.risk_of_conflict: typing a shifting API surface wastes effort
edges.example: fix API surface before typing it

edges.why_related: the checker validates the authored hints
edges.benefit_of_coupling: hints enable a meaningful type gate
edges.risk_of_conflict: running the checker before hints exist yields no signal

edges.why_related: public behavior to test follows from scope/layout
edges.risk_of_conflict: testing undefined behavior churns tests

edges.why_related: fixtures support the designed tests
edges.risk_of_conflict: building fixtures before tests exist is speculative

edges.why_related: fixtures often manage resources via context managers
edges.risk_of_conflict: fixtures without cleanup discipline leak resources

edges.why_related: TDD is a discipline applied to the pytest suite
edges.risk_of_conflict: TDD without suite conventions is unstructured

edges.why_related: coverage measures the existing suite
edges.risk_of_conflict: coverage with no suite is meaningless

edges.why_related: the project root and python version frame the env
edges.risk_of_conflict: creating env before target python churns it

edges.why_related: resolution runs inside the isolated env
edges.risk_of_conflict: resolving in system python pollutes globally

edges.why_related: app-vs-library scope shapes pinning strategy
edges.risk_of_conflict: pinning before scope decided causes rework

edges.why_related: the lockfile pins the resolved set
edges.risk_of_conflict: locking before a valid resolution pins a broken set

edges.why_related: resolution and lock needs constrain tool choice
edges.risk_of_conflict: choosing a tool that cannot lock blocks reproducibility
edges.example: let needs bound the tool choice

edges.why_related: metadata encodes the layout and naming decisions
edges.risk_of_conflict: writing metadata before layout churns it

edges.why_related: declared dependencies populate the metadata
edges.risk_of_conflict: metadata deps before resolution are guesses

edges.why_related: the build backend reads pyproject metadata
edges.benefit_of_coupling: valid metadata enables a clean build
edges.risk_of_conflict: building without valid metadata fails

edges.why_related: entry points and extras are declared in pyproject
edges.risk_of_conflict: declaring entry points before metadata is impossible

edges.why_related: publishing uploads the built artifacts
edges.benefit_of_coupling: valid artifacts enable a clean publish
edges.risk_of_conflict: publishing before a valid build ships nothing usable

edges.why_related: the release version labels the published artifact
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a correct version gates the publish
edges.risk_of_conflict: publishing without a version policy mislabels releases

edges.why_related: the built artifact's API diff informs the version bump
edges.risk_of_conflict: versioning without seeing the artifact misjudges the bump

edges.why_related: a reproducible locked env should back the release build
edges.benefit_of_coupling: locked env makes release builds reproducible
edges.risk_of_conflict: publishing from an unlocked env is irreproducible
edges.example: lock the build env before publishing

edges.why_related: CI runs the test suite as a gate
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a suite enables the CI test gate
edges.risk_of_conflict: automating release without tests gates nothing
edges.example: build tests before the CI gate

edges.why_related: CI runs the type checker as a gate
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a configured checker enables the CI type gate
edges.risk_of_conflict: automating release without a type gate ships type regressions

edges.why_related: CI builds the artifacts in the pipeline
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a working build enables automated build steps
edges.risk_of_conflict: automating a build that fails locally is futile
edges.example: make build work before automating it

edges.why_related: CI performs the publish step
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a working publish enables automated publishing
edges.risk_of_conflict: automating a broken publish leaks bad releases
edges.example: make publish work before automating it

edges.why_related: dependency freshness pulls against locked reproducibility
edges.risk_of_conflict: chasing latest breaks reproducible builds; over-locking ships stale CVEs
edges.example: schedule controlled lock refreshes with revalidation
edges.resolution_rule: reproducibility dominates day-to-day; scheduled refresh reconciles

edges.why_related: release velocity pressures correct compatibility labeling
edges.risk_of_conflict: rushing a publish mislabels a breaking change as minor
edges.example: block publish until API diff classifies the bump

edges.why_related: type-checking effort competes with test-writing effort for finite QA time
edges.benefit_of_coupling: allocate QA effort across typing and tests
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-investing one starves the other and leaves a gap
edges.example: cover behavior with tests; types document and guard interfaces
edges.resolution_rule: behavioral risk areas get tests first; types cover interface contracts

edges.why_related: coverage targets can distort the TDD intent of specifying behavior
edges.benefit_of_coupling: keep coverage a signal, not the goal
edges.risk_of_conflict: chasing a coverage number produces weak assertion-free tests
edges.example: treat coverage as a gap finder, not a target
edges.resolution_rule: behavior specification dominates the coverage number

edges.why_related: tool-specific config can fragment standard pyproject metadata
edges.benefit_of_coupling: prefer standard fields over tool-locked config
edges.risk_of_conflict: tool-proprietary sections reduce portability of metadata
edges.example: keep PEP-standard metadata canonical; tool config additive

edges.why_related: the lockfile must stay consistent with declared metadata constraints
edges.risk_of_conflict: a lock diverging from metadata is unverifiable
edges.example: regenerate lock from current metadata only

edges.why_related: typing protocols constrain how the data model is expressed
edges.risk_of_conflict: mistyped protocols misrepresent the data model
edges.example: align hints with actual protocol behavior

edges.why_related: a defective published release triggers a new version bump
edges.risk_of_conflict: an immutable bad release forces a superseding version
edges.example: on defect, yank and increment; stop when a clean version is published
edges.resolution_rule: feedback stops once a corrected version ships

edges.why_related: coverage gaps trigger adding or revising tests
edges.risk_of_conflict: uncovered critical paths signal missing tests
edges.example: add tests for uncovered risk; stop when critical paths covered
edges.resolution_rule: feedback stops when critical-path coverage met

edges.why_related: resolution stability changes the probability of green CI builds
edges.risk_of_conflict: flaky resolution causes intermittent CI failures
edges.example: pin via lock to stabilize CI resolution

edges.why_related: isolation quality changes how reproducible a locked install is
edges.risk_of_conflict: leaky env makes a lock non-reproducible
edges.example: build and verify locks in a clean isolated env

conflict_axes.trigger: wanting the latest dependency versions conflicts with byte-reproducible locked builds
resolution_order: keep the lockfile authoritative for builds
refresh dependencies on a controlled schedule
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: reproducibility governs build-time; freshness is admitted only through reviewed, revalidated lock refreshes
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a security advisory affects a pinned dependency
conflict_axes.example: keeping a CVE-affected pin to preserve reproducibility

conflict_axes.trigger: finite QA effort must be split between type checking and behavioral tests
resolution_order: cover high-risk behavior with tests first
use types to guard and document interfaces
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: behavioral correctness of risky paths dominates; static typing covers interface contracts and refactor safety
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a risk area has neither tests nor types
conflict_axes.example: relying only on types while a critical path is untested

conflict_axes.trigger: convenient tool-proprietary config competes with portable PEP-standard metadata
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: standard metadata dominates; tool-specific config may extend but not replace canonical fields
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a tool requires non-portable metadata that others cannot read
conflict_axes.example: encoding dependencies only in a tool-proprietary section

conflict_axes.trigger: pressure to ship fast competes with correctly classifying breaking changes
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: compatibility correctness dominates release speed; a publish is blocked until the bump level is justified
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a breaking change would otherwise ship as a minor/patch
conflict_axes.example: rushing a release that mislabels an API break

conflict_axes.trigger: high checker strictness can slow iteration during exploratory development
resolution_order: set strictness to the risk of the surface
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: release-surface strictness dominates at release; exploratory code may run looser with a tightening gate
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if loose strictness reaches a published interface
conflict_axes.example: shipping a public API typed mostly as Any

conflict_axes.trigger: chasing a coverage number competes with writing genuinely valuable tests
resolution_order: treat coverage as a gap finder
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: behavioral value dominates; coverage is a diagnostic signal, never the optimization target
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if tests are added only to raise the number

conflict_axes.trigger: flat layout is simpler but can let tests import the in-tree copy instead of the installed package
resolution_order: run tests against the installed package
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: import-correctness of the installed artifact dominates; src-layout is preferred where shadowing is a risk
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if tests pass locally but the installed package fails to import
conflict_axes.example: tests importing the source tree, masking a packaging bug

conflict_axes.trigger: applications want tight pins while libraries need broad constraints for downstream compatibility
resolution_order: classify the project as app or library
pin tightly for apps via lockfile
use broad bounded constraints for libraries
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the project classification dominates: libraries must not over-pin, applications must lock; semver bounds guide library breadth
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a library over-pins and breaks downstream resolution
conflict_axes.example: a published library pinning an exact transitive version

edge_cases.trigger: a defective artifact is uploaded to the index
edge_cases.failure_mode: irreversible publish of a broken release
edge_cases.example: a wheel that fails to import is published to PyPI and cannot be overwritten
edge_cases.detection_method: TestPyPI install check and twine metadata validation before the real upload

edge_cases.trigger: the lockfile no longer matches the manifest
edge_cases.example: manifest gains a dependency but the lock is not regenerated
edge_cases.detection_method: CI check that the lock is consistent with the manifest and hashes verify
resolution: regenerate the lock from the current manifest

edge_cases.failure_mode: resolver cannot find a valid set
edge_cases.example: two pins require incompatible versions of a shared transitive dependency
edge_cases.detection_method: run the resolver and inspect the conflict report
resolution: relax or rebound the conflicting constraints

edge_cases.trigger: a needed non-code file is not included in the wheel
edge_cases.example: package data omitted from build config so a template file is absent after install
edge_cases.detection_method: install the built wheel into a clean venv and import/run it
resolution: add the data file to the build manifest

edge_cases.trigger: a breaking change ships under a non-major bump
edge_cases.example: a removed public function released as a patch breaks importers
edge_cases.detection_method: diff the public API against the prior release before assigning the bump

edge_cases.example: pip install run without an activated venv hits the system interpreter
edge_cases.detection_method: check that the active interpreter is the project venv before installing

edge_cases.trigger: hints describe a contract the code does not honor
edge_cases.failure_mode: false confidence from passing type check
edge_cases.example: a function annotated to return str sometimes returns None
edge_cases.detection_method: run the checker at adequate strictness and add runtime tests on the contract
resolution: correct the annotation or the implementation

edge_cases.example: a session-scoped mutable fixture couples unrelated tests
edge_cases.detection_method: run tests in randomized order and detect order-dependence

edge_cases.trigger: index credentials exposed in CI logs or config
edge_cases.example: an upload token printed in a CI log
edge_cases.detection_method: scan CI config and logs for secrets; prefer trusted publishing over stored tokens

edge_cases.trigger: pyproject.toml is malformed or missing build-system
edge_cases.example: a TOML syntax error or absent [build-system] table
edge_cases.detection_method: parse pyproject and run a build in CI
resolution: fix the metadata or build-system table

edge_cases.example: 100% line coverage where tests assert nothing meaningful
edge_cases.detection_method: review assertion density and mutation-style spot checks on critical paths
resolution: stop treating the number as the goal

edge_cases.trigger: an entry point references a missing or wrong callable
edge_cases.example: a console_scripts target points to a function that does not exist
edge_cases.detection_method: install the wheel and invoke the declared command/plugin
resolution: reinstall and verify the command runs

workflow.objective: fix scope, app-vs-library classification, layout, and public API surface
workflow.do_first_because: every packaging and typing decision inherits scope, layout, and API surface

exit_criteria: idiomatic implementation complete for the surface
workflow.do_first_because: downstream typing and tests operate on the implemented language constructs

workflow.objective: type the interfaces and gate them with a static checker
workflow.do_first_because: typed contracts catch interface errors before tests and packaging

workflow.objective: establish a behavior-focused, isolated, measured test suite
workflow.do_first_because: a trustworthy suite gates every later build and release

workflow.objective: isolate the environment, declare constraints, and resolve a dependency set
acceptance_tests: constraints resolve to a valid set
exit_criteria: resolution succeeds in an isolated env
workflow.do_first_because: a stable resolved environment is the basis for locking and reproducible builds

workflow.objective: pin the resolved graph in a hashed lockfile
workflow.do_first_because: reproducible installs must be fixed before packaging and publishing

workflow.objective: author metadata and build installable wheels/sdists with correct interfaces
acceptance_tests: wheel installs and imports in a clean venv
workflow.do_first_because: publishing requires valid metadata and verified installable artifacts

workflow.objective: classify the change and assign a semver bump
inputs_required: public API diff vs prior release
acceptance_tests: bump level matches the change class
workflow.do_first_because: a correct version must label the artifact before it is published immutably

workflow.objective: automate the validated pipeline and publish to the index after gates pass
entry_criteria: tests/types green, artifacts built, version assigned, lock verified
acceptance_tests: trusted publishing or scoped token used
human review recorded for the publish
workflow.do_first_because: this is the only irreversible step and must run last behind all gates and human review

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible or high-risk step is pressured to ship fast
dominance_rules.rule: risk and irreversibility control dominates speed for publish-class steps
dominance_rules.required_action: gate the step behind tests, validation, and review before proceeding
dominance_rules.example: holding a PyPI publish until TestPyPI and metadata checks pass

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node is not yet unblocked by its prerequisites
dominance_rules.rule: true dependency precedence dominates value-first ordering
dominance_rules.required_action: schedule prerequisites before dependents regardless of standalone value
dominance_rules.example: building wheels only after pyproject metadata is valid

dominance_rules.trigger: dependency freshness conflicts with reproducible builds
dominance_rules.rule: reproducibility dominates at build time; freshness enters only via reviewed lock refreshes
dominance_rules.required_action: build from the committed lockfile and refresh on a controlled schedule
dominance_rules.example: keeping the locked set for the release build and refreshing separately

dominance_rules.trigger: release speed pressures correct semver classification
dominance_rules.required_action: compute and review the public API diff before assigning the bump
dominance_rules.example: reclassifying a removed function as a major bump despite schedule pressure

dominance_rules.trigger: a node is being locked before its tests or checks pass
dominance_rules.required_action: pass acceptance tests and validation before any soft or hard lock
dominance_rules.example: refusing to hard-lock a release until CI is green

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible or high-risk decision would be automated
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for irreversible/high-risk steps
dominance_rules.required_action: require recorded human approval before the irreversible action
dominance_rules.example: a person approves the PyPI upload even in an automated pipeline

dominance_rules.trigger: metadata schema stability conflicts with adding more config
dominance_rules.rule: standard metadata-schema stability dominates volume of tool-specific config
dominance_rules.required_action: keep PEP-standard fields canonical and add tool config additively
dominance_rules.example: declaring dependencies in standard pyproject rather than a proprietary section

dominance_rules.trigger: a numeric estimate is presented as more certain than its evidence
dominance_rules.required_action: label all estimates heuristic and avoid implying measured certainty
dominance_rules.example: marking resolver reliability as heuristic, not observed, with no dataset

dominance_rules.trigger: output formatting competes with strict machine-parseable structure
dominance_rules.rule: strict JSON validity dominates prose quality
dominance_rules.required_action: emit strict JSON only with closed enums and no placeholders
dominance_rules.example: returning the KB as raw JSON with no markdown fences

dominance_rules.trigger: a locally optimal step would create downstream rework
dominance_rules.required_action: order work so upstream foundations stabilize before dependents
dominance_rules.example: fixing layout before writing imports and entry points

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix scope, layout, and public API surface before any packaging work
anti_rework_rules.rationale: packaging a shifting layout/API forces metadata and import rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: metadata or imports rewritten after a layout change
anti_rework_rules.example: authoring pyproject before deciding src vs flat layout

anti_rework_rules.rule: resolve scope before populating packaging schema/metadata
anti_rework_rules.rationale: metadata built on undecided scope is discarded
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: app/library classification changes after metadata written
anti_rework_rules.example: tightening pins before deciding app vs library

anti_rework_rules.rule: author type hints before running the static checker
anti_rework_rules.rationale: running the checker with no hints yields no signal and wasted config
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: checker run produces no meaningful diagnostics
anti_rework_rules.example: configuring mypy strict on an unannotated module

anti_rework_rules.rule: build the test suite before measuring coverage
anti_rework_rules.rationale: coverage of an empty or thin suite is meaningless
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: coverage reported with almost no tests

anti_rework_rules.rule: resolve a valid dependency set before generating a lockfile
anti_rework_rules.rationale: locking a broken or partial resolution pins an unusable set
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: lockfile generated from a failed resolution
anti_rework_rules.example: committing a lock before the resolver succeeds

anti_rework_rules.rule: create an isolated environment before resolving and installing
anti_rework_rules.rationale: resolving in system python pollutes globals and is irreproducible
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: packages installed into the system interpreter
anti_rework_rules.example: pip install run with no venv active

anti_rework_rules.rule: author valid pyproject metadata before building artifacts
anti_rework_rules.rationale: building without valid metadata fails or produces broken wheels
anti_rework_rules.example: running a build with no build-system table

anti_rework_rules.rule: build and verify installable artifacts before publishing
anti_rework_rules.rationale: publishing an unverified artifact ships an irreversible broken release
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: upload performed before a clean-install check
anti_rework_rules.example: uploading a wheel never installed in a clean venv

anti_rework_rules.rule: classify and assign the version before publishing
blocked_until: bump level justified by API diff
anti_rework_rules.rationale: publishing without a justified version mislabels compatibility immutably
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: release uploaded with an unjustified version
anti_rework_rules.example: shipping a breaking change as a patch

anti_rework_rules.rule: pass tests, types, and validation before hard-locking the release
blocked_until: all gates green and review recorded
anti_rework_rules.rationale: hard-locking before gates pass risks shipping defects irreversibly
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: release hard-locked while CI is red
anti_rework_rules.example: tagging a release before CI gates pass

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or CI reports a failure
iteration_protocol.detection: compare validation_report checks and CI gates to thresholds
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

action: score defects by risk and irreversibility
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only sub-threshold low-risk defects remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: a fix touches a high-coupling or locked node
acceptance_tests: all dependents of the change identified

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is assigned for repair
iteration_protocol.detection: map failure type to repair_routing subsystem
action: apply the repair via the formula script or reference fix
acceptance_tests: repair applied by the correct subsystem

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence or a status change affects importance
iteration_protocol.detection: recompute posterior and compare to revisit delta
acceptance_tests: posterior recomputed consistently with the formula
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: posterior change below the revisit delta

iteration_protocol.trigger: an upstream node changes after dependents were locked
iteration_protocol.detection: detect upstream change against lock state
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no locked dependent has an unreviewed upstream change

iteration_protocol.trigger: risk or irreversibility crosses the human-review threshold
acceptance_tests: decision recorded with approver and risk acceptance
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: human approval recorded or action rejected

human_review_required_for: semantic-version bump classification for breaking changes

checks.repair_action: modeled freshness-vs-reproducibility and typing-vs-testing tensions as conflict edges, not dependencies
derived fields recomputed by formula script
